January 21, 1999

Libertarian Party denounces arrest of medical marijuana activist Steve Kubby, requests help for legal defense fund

WASHINGTON, DC—The arrest of medical marijuana activist and former Libertarian gubernatorial candidate Steve Kubby is not just a cruel attack on a cancer patient—it’s a crime against California voters, the Libertarian Party says.

"By continuing to arrest sick and dying cancer patients despite overwhelming public approval for Proposition 215, California authorities are flouting the will of the voters," said Steve Dasbach, national director of the Libertarian Party. "They should drop their prosecution of Steve Kubby—and every other medical marijuana patient in California."

Kubby, 52, was the 1998 Libertarian candidate for governor of California and is an outspoken advocate of medical marijuana. He and his wife Michele, 32, were arrested Tuesday when a dozen agents of the North Tahoe Narcotics Task Force raided their home in Olympic Valley, near Lake Tahoe, California. They were taken to Placer County Jail, where bail was originally set at $100,000 each. The Kubbys were charged with unauthorized cultivation, harvesting and processing of marijuana; possession with intent to sell; and conspiracy.

On Thursday they were released on their own recognizance following arraignment in Tahoe City Court. The Kubbys are due back in court on January 28th for a preliminary hearing where they are expected to enter a not guilty plea.

Kubby played a key role in Proposition 215, overwhelmingly approved by voters in November 1996, which allows seriously ill patients to grow and use marijuana with a doctor’s recommendation.

Noting that Steve Kubby was diagnosed with adrenal cancer in 1975 and uses medical marijuana under doctor’s orders, Dasbach said, "Proposition 215 was written and passed with people like Kubby in mind. By throwing cancer patients in jail, California prosecutors have arrogantly substituted their judgment for that of physicians and voters."

Mark Hinkle, state chair of the California Libertarian Party, said: "This arrest is an outrage and a slap across the faces of California voters. Steve and Michele Kubby are law-abiding citizens and the police have no authority to raid their home, throw them in jail, and jeopardize Steve’s health."

Before the Kubbys were taken into custody they reportedly presented officers with their patient credentials and notes from physicians. Kubby told friends that an officer remarked, "That 215 doesn’t apply here. Maybe it’ll work in San Francisco, but not out here."

"California residents must be wondering whether local police will be enforcing all laws at random, or just those governing medical marijuana," Dasbach said. "Are murder, rape, and robbery still illegal statewide, or just in the cities where police decide to prosecute those crimes?"

Tuesday’s arrest is the second time in six months that California authorities have prosecuted a prominent Libertarian Party member for using medical marijuana, Dasbach noted. "At the Libertarian Party’s national convention in July, best-selling author Peter McWilliams blasted the federal government’s vendetta against medical marijuana in a speech broadcast live on C-Span," he said. "Just 19 days later, he was arrested for the ‘crime’ of growing marijuana to distribute to sick people under the state’s medical marijuana law."

Arresting users of medical marijuana isn’t just illegal and immoral, Dasbach said—it’s also dangerous. "How many murderers, rapists, and child molesters will go free as police spend their time— and your money—raiding the homes of law-abiding citizens to see whether they’re taking their doctor-prescribed medical marijuana?" Dasbach asked. "Do police in Lake Tahoe want to accept responsibility for the violent crimes that will occur as a result of this diversion of police resources?"

Dasbach emphasized that California’s prosecution of medical marijuana users could have national implications.

"Last November voters in at least four states—Nevada, Alaska, Arizona, and Washington state—overwhelmingly passed laws approving of medical marijuana," he said. "Police and prosecutors in those states need to know that they can’t get away with trampling the will of their voters, California-style."

The Kubby arrests have already generated news articles by the Associated Press, United Press International, the Los Angeles Times and the Orange County Register, which published an editorial on Thursday calling the arrests "an outrage" and urging authorities to start respecting the will of the voters on Proposition 215.

Now it’s time to capitalize on that publicity, Dasbach said.

"First, contact California Attorney General Bill Lockyer and ask him to intervene. He has said publicly that he voted for Proposition 215 and wants to find a way to ‘make it work.’ Politely let him know that he can do that by demanding that local authorities start following the law—and drop the prosecution of the Kubbys. By doing so he can send a message to his counterparts in other states that the will of the voters must be respected.

"Second, contribute to the Kubby Defense Fund to help Steve and Michele pay the legal costs of defending themselves against this unjust prosecution."

LIBERTARIAN CANDIDATE AND WIFE FREED FROM JAIL

PARTY URGES LOCKYER TO INVESTIGATE

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Jan. 21 /PRNewswire/ -- Steve Kubby, the 1998 Libertarian candidate for governor of California, and his wife Michele were released on their own recognizance from police custody today following arraignment in Tahoe City Court.

The Kubbys were arrested Tuesday morning in a police raid of their home in Olympic Valley. They are charged with unauthorized cultivation, harvesting, and processing of marijuana; possession with intent to sell; and conspiracy.

"We are relieved and grateful that Steve and Michele Kubby have been freed from custody," announced Libertarian state chair Mark Hinkle. "They have broken no laws and should never have been arrested in the first place."

Steve played a pivotal role in the November, 1996, passage of Prop. 215, the medical marijuana initiative. He takes medical marijuana under doctor’s orders to treat adrenal cancer, which he was diagnosed with in 1975, and hypertension. Michele also takes medical marijuana to alleviate the symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome.

The Kubbys are due back in court on January 28th for a preliminary hearing where they are expected to enter a not guilty plea.

The Libertarian Party of California, responding to the Kubbys’ arrest and incarceration, drafted a sternly-worded letter to state Attorney General Bill Lockyer "on behalf of the 5,382,915 Californians who voted in favor of Proposition 215," urging Lockyer to intervene in the case.

In the letter, the party called on Lockyer "to bring the full weight of your office down in this matter and investigate the North Tahoe Task Force and Placer County District Attorney’s office to determine the cause of this unnecessary police action."

"Mr. Lockyer swore to uphold the laws of the state of California when he was inaugurated earlier this month. We are simply asking him to do so in this case," stated Hinkle. "Prop. 215 was passed by the voters of this state over two years ago. It is a disgrace that law enforcement continues to ignore the will of the voters and prosecute law-abiding citizens who are using a form of medicine that is completely legal."

Response to the Kubbys’ arrest has been overwhelming, according to Hinkle. "The flood of emails, phone calls, and faxes has been unbelievably supportive of the Kubbys. Californians are outraged that the government can so flagrantly ignore the law and jeopardize someone’s health.

"What has happened to the Kubbys is a sobering reminder that liberty comes at a price."
